notes: To **sign out**, use your name at the bottom of the menu. The session also expires on its own after 8 hours.

callouts.body: The **current weight** is saved as the pet's current weight and adds a point to the trend chart on its record. The **medications used** are deducted from inventory stock automatically — there's no separate movement to record.
callouts.title: Two fields that do more than they look

callouts.body: The system checks stock *before* creating the visit. If a medication isn't enough, it tells you and doesn't save: that way you're never left with a half-recorded visit. Add the stock under Inventory and try again.
callouts.title: If stock runs short, nothing is saved

care.intro: The clinical record of what was done to the pet.
notes: Once saved, the visit is **awaiting payment** and shows up on its own on the Payments screen.

steps.description: The screen starts with a search box. Typing the national ID brings up all of that person's pets and you pick one.
steps.title: Look the pet up by its owner's national ID

steps.description: Below, previous visits are listed with diagnosis, treatment, weight and amount.
steps.title: Review its history

steps.description: Service type, diagnosis and treatment are required. External tests, current weight and the medications used are optional.
steps.title: Press “New visit”

care.title: Medical care

callouts.body: Click any row in the list to open it. It brings together the details, a weight trend chart (it only appears with two or more measurements) and a timeline of everything that happened to that pet: visits, vaccines, appointments and even the corrections someone made to its details.
callouts.title: The pet's record

callouts.body: Deleting a pet takes it out of the lists and search, but its history is kept and you can reactivate it from its own record. To see it again, switch on “Show inactive” in the list. This is deliberate: really deleting it would mean losing the visits and payments attached to it.
callouts.title: “Delete” doesn't really delete

clients.intro: Owners aren't created on their own: they come into being when you register their first pet.
notes: Under **Owners** you edit a client's name, phone and address, and see their pets as clickable tags. The national ID can't be edited: it's the key used to look that person up everywhere in the system.

steps.description: The first thing it asks for is the owner's national ID.
steps.title: Go to Pets → “New pet”

steps.description: If that person is already registered, the system recognises them and fills in their details: no duplicate. If they're new, it asks for their name, surname and phone.
steps.title: Type the national ID and wait a second

steps.description: Name, species and sex are required. Breed, date of birth and weight are optional, but the date of birth is what lets the age show, and the weight feeds the trend chart.
steps.title: Fill in the pet's details

clients.title: Clients and pets

dayToDay.intro: The usual path of a client who walks in, from start to finish.
notes: You don't have to follow the whole path: a pet can be seen without an appointment, or registered today and booked in next week. The only linked step is payment — **recording a visit automatically creates an outstanding payment**, and that's the list Reception sees under Payments.
dayToDay.title: A day in the clinic

faq.answer: Check you haven't already taken payment: once paid it leaves “Awaiting payment” and moves to “Latest payments”. If it still doesn't show, reload the screen.
faq.question: I recorded a visit but it isn't showing under Payments

faq.answer: That vet has no working hours set for that day of the week. Set them under Schedule → Working hours. If you're a vet, remember you can only book for yourself.
faq.question: It won't let me book: there are no slots available

faq.answer: Pets can be “deleted”, but it's reversible: they're hidden and can be reactivated. Medications with recorded movements aren't deleted, because that would break the inventory history.
faq.question: Why can't I delete a pet or a medication?

faq.answer: That's expected for now: the clinic's bank API isn't connected yet. Charge with your bank's own QR outside the system and record the payment here with the “QR” method.
faq.question: Charging by QR gives me an error

faq.answer: Their account is probably deactivated or pending approval. Check under Users: the lists for booking and seeing pets only offer active vets.
faq.question: A vet isn't in the list when I try to book

faq.answer: Yes. Every screen adapts: on phones and tablets the listings show as cards instead of tables, so they read without scrolling sideways, and the menu opens with the three-line button. You can also install it as an app from the browser menu.
faq.question: Can I use PawCare on a phone or tablet?

faq.answer: Sending email requires the clinic to have set it up. If it doesn't arrive, the Administrator can create the account directly, or reset the password from Users and pass it on in person.
faq.question: The invitation or password recovery email never arrived

faq.answer: The data the clinic enters — pet names, breeds, diagnoses, notes — is shown exactly as it was typed: the system translates its own interface, not the content. WhatsApp messages are also always in Spanish, because the client is the one reading them.
faq.question: I switched the language but some text is still in Spanish

callouts.body: Press **Ctrl + K** (or **⌘ + K** on a Mac), or the “Search…” button above the menu. Type a pet's name, or an owner's name, surname or national ID, and it takes you straight to their record. It works from any screen and saves you guessing where to look.
callouts.title: Search is the fastest shortcut

callouts.body: The “Forgot your password?” link on the sign-in screen sends an email, so it only works if your account has an email on file *and* the clinic has set up email sending. If not, ask the Administrator to reset it from Users: they'll pass it on to you in person.
callouts.title: If you forgot your password

gettingStarted.intro: How to sign in and find your way around.

steps.description: It isn't your email: it's a username the clinic's Administrator assigns. If you get it wrong, the system won't tell you which of the two fields failed — that's deliberate, for security.
steps.title: Sign in with the username you were given

steps.description: It's the first screen. At the top it shows the current numbers (registered pets, today's appointments, outstanding payments) and below it, shortcuts to the modules your role can use.
steps.title: Check the Home screen

steps.description: It's grouped into four sections: Clients, Clinic, Administration and System. You only see the modules for your role. On a phone the menu opens with the three-line button.
steps.title: Use the menu on the left

gettingStarted.title: Getting started

callouts.body: If it already has movements (stock added or used), the system won't let it be deleted: it would make part of the history disappear. Only the ones never used can be deleted.
callouts.title: Why a medication sometimes can't be deleted

callouts.body: When a batch expires its units **stop being available** even if they are still on the shelf: they cannot be used in a visit and do not count towards the minimum stock. You will see a red alert with the batch and how many units are left — take them off the shelf. When a medication is used the system always draws from **the batch expiring soonest**, so nothing expires waiting its turn.
callouts.title: Expired stock stops counting

inventory.intro: Medication stock, and its alert when something is about to run out.

steps.description: That's the alert threshold. When current stock drops to it or below, the medication is flagged “Low stock” and is added to the warning at the top.
steps.title: Set a minimum stock for each medication

steps.description: The «Record entry» button asks for the quantity and, optionally, the batch number and expiry date. Each entry becomes its own batch: with no date, the system cannot warn you when that batch is about to expire.
steps.title: Add stock when a delivery arrives

steps.description: Every time a visit uses a medication, the stock goes down automatically.
steps.title: Stock going out records itself

inventory.title: Inventory

callouts.body: Every payment gets its own number (**R-2026-000042**) that never changes. It's printed on the PDF and stored in the system, so weeks later you can re-issue it from “Latest payments” with the **Receipt** button on each row. The receipt is internal to the clinic: **it does not replace a tax invoice**.
callouts.title: The receipt number is the answer to “you never charged me for that”

callouts.body: It generates a real bank QR, but that needs the clinic's bank API connected, and that isn't done yet. Today the button shows a message explaining exactly that, instead of a fake QR nobody could pay. **To charge by QR in the meantime**, use your bank's own QR outside the system and record the payment here choosing the “QR” method.
callouts.title: The “Charge by QR” button doesn't charge yet

payments.intro: Everything that's been seen and not yet paid, in a single list.

steps.description: At the top of the screen: how much is left to collect in total, and how many visits make it up.
steps.title: Look at the outstanding total

steps.description: You pick the method (Cash, Card, Transfer or QR) and confirm the amount. The visit becomes paid and drops off the outstanding list.
steps.title: Press “Take payment” on the right row

steps.description: As soon as the payment goes through, the screen shows the receipt with its number. From there you can download it as a PDF or send it to the client on WhatsApp with the details already written.
steps.title: Hand over the receipt

steps.description: The five most recent payments, with their method and date.
steps.title: Check “Latest payments”

payments.title: Payments

callouts.body: Care with no next-dose date still saves, but it will **never show up** under “Due in the next 30 days”, and it won't generate a reminder. Fill it in whenever you know it.
callouts.title: No next dose, no reminder

callouts.body: If you recorded **which vaccine you gave and the vial's batch**, they are printed on the card. If you didn't, that box is left blank to fill in by hand — as are older doses, recorded before the system stored it. The **signature and stamp** box is always left empty: that one is done by hand and is what makes another clinic trust the paper. The card also carries ruled blank rows so it stays usable after printing. **It is not enough to travel abroad**: SENASAG's zoosanitary certificate is also required, and that is exactly where the rabies vaccine's brand and batch get asked for.
callouts.title: The card is finished by hand, and that is on purpose

preventive.intro: Preventive care keeps track of what was given and when the next dose is due.

steps.description: The first thing you see: the care whose next dose falls within the next 30 days. Anything past its date carries an “Overdue” tag in red.
steps.title: The “Due in the next 30 days” panel

steps.description: Same as under Medical care, to see its full preventive history.
steps.title: Look a pet up by its owner's national ID

steps.description: Pick Vaccine or Deworming, the date it was given and — strongly recommended — the date of the next dose.
steps.title: Record the care

steps.description: The “Download card” button builds the card as a PDF: the pet's and owner's details, and two records — vaccination and deworming — with the doses in order and overdue ones in red. The same button is on the pet's file.
steps.title: Download the card

preventive.title: Vaccines and deworming

callouts.body: The system works out who needs a nudge and drafts the message, but someone has to open the screen and click. It never sends anything on its own. The message is always in Spanish, because the clinic's client is the one reading it.
callouts.title: Sending is manual, not automatic

reminders.intro: Nudges to clients over WhatsApp, to cut down on no-shows.

steps.description: The system builds the list on its own: appointments in the next 24 hours and preventive care due within 7 days.
steps.title: Open Reminders

steps.description: WhatsApp opens with the owner's number and the message already written. You can edit it before sending.
steps.title: Press “Send on WhatsApp”

steps.description: That's what takes the client off the list and stops them being messaged twice. It's recorded under “Recently sent”.
steps.title: Come back and press “Mark as sent”

reminders.title: Reminders

callouts.body: Each report has buttons to download it as Excel or PDF, with whatever filters you have set. On top of that, Settings has “Export all my data”: an Excel file with one sheet per kind of information in the system.
callouts.title: Everything can be exported

cards.description: Every payment taken, with filters by date range, service type and payment method. At the top it shows the total and how many payments match those filters.
cards.title: Revenue

cards.description: Two views: the visits over a period, and a chart of revenue grouped by service type, which answers which service brings in the most.
cards.title: Clinical and administrative

reports.intro: Administrator only. Two views of the same information.
reports.title: Reports

callouts.body: A **Vet can only book and reschedule appointments for themselves**. The Administrator and Reception can do it for any vet. Same with working hours: a vet edits their own, not their colleagues'.
callouts.title: The rule that surprises people most

roles.intro: There are three roles. The menu only shows you the modules for your role, and the server turns down any request for data outside it: if you reached someone else's screen, you'd see no data, only an error.
roles.title: What each role does

callouts.body: Almost always it's because **that vet has no working hours set for that day** of the week. Go to the “Working hours” tab, switch on the right shift and try again. A vet with no hours that day simply has no slots to offer.
callouts.title: If no slots are available

callouts.body: It doesn't change the pet or the vet: for that, cancel and book a new one. And a cancelled appointment can't be rescheduled. You also can't put two appointments with the same vet at the same time — the system blocks it.
callouts.title: Rescheduling only moves the date and time

schedule.intro: Appointments and working hours live on the same screen, because each vet's hours are what decide which slots are free.

from.description: The state every new appointment starts in
from.label: Confirmed

to.description: The pet came in and was seen
to.label: Attended

to.description: It didn't happen; the slot is free again
to.label: Cancelled

steps.description: Pick the pet, the vet, the consultation type and the date. Available slots appear grouped into Morning and Afternoon; booked ones are disabled.
steps.title: The “New Appointment” tab

steps.description: The schedule grouped by day. From each appointment you can reschedule it, mark it attended or cancel it.
steps.title: The “Appointments” tab

steps.description: Each vet's weekly grid, with up to two shifts a day (morning and afternoon). Reception doesn't see this tab.
steps.title: The “Working hours” tab

schedule.title: Schedule

callouts.body: **Signed in** is a successful entry. **Wrong credentials** can be a forgotten password or a username that doesn't even exist — that attempt is recorded too, with whatever was typed — and **Deactivated account** is someone with a suspended account trying to get in. The person signing in always gets the same message with no hints: the difference is only recorded here.
callouts.title: What each outcome means

callouts.body: Accounts aren't deleted, they're deactivated: someone deactivated can't sign in and drops off the lists for booking or seeing pets, but their history stays intact. Reactivate them whenever it's needed.
callouts.title: Deactivate instead of deleting

cards.description: “New user” asks for the details and the role. If you pick Vet, two more fields appear: license number and specialty.
cards.title: Create an account

cards.description: “Invite a vet” emails them a link to fill in their own details. The account is active as soon as they accept.
cards.title: Invite a vet

cards.description: A vet can request access themselves, from the link on the sign-in screen. They show up as “Pending approval” and can't get in until you press “Approve”.
cards.title: Approve a request

cards.description: The second tab records who activated, deactivated, changed a role, reset a password or invited someone, and when.
cards.title: Audit log

cards.description: The third tab records **every sign-in attempt**: who got in, when, from which IP address and with which browser. Failed attempts too — if someone has been trying passwords, you'll see it here.
cards.title: Sign-ins
